writer_specific_bindings.abstract: We give a negative answer to Kurose's Question 3(e) in the 1998 collection Open Problems in Affine Differential Geometry and Related Topics. For the product S²(1) × ℝ with its product metric and Levi–Civita connection, every radial orthogonal distribution in that question is integrable, but the dual statistical structure is nowhere locally 1-conformally flat. Integrability follows from the first variation of energy; nonflatness follows from two curvature evaluations. A conformal metric and projective connection change also give an example with nowhere zero cubic tensor. The same obstruction works in every dimension at least three. The proof is independent of computation. Historical priority is unresolved; no claim of a first resolution is made.

writer_specific_bindings.abstract: We construct a bounded-degree physical tree model in which the normalized marginal admitted demand drops from one to zero while the spare-capacity graph changes from the entire tree to isolated vertices. Capacities arise from the unique cheapest fixed-topology enlargement supporting doubled initial traffic. Each of the k² cross-root streams has an independent, fixed-law exponential growth rate. An all-cuts estimate confines both changes, with probability tending to one, to an interval of width 16√(log k/k) around mean doubled demand. Both outer-phase conclusions hold for every optimizer. This is a specialized existence response to Aldous's conceptual congestion toy-model request. The width is an upper bound; no critical profile or universal traffic law is asserted.
